newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Black Sea Energy sets Russia oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Black Sea Energy sets Russia oil deal.

text.p: Black Sea Energy Ltd said it completed necessary agreements in Krasnodar and Moscow to form a joint venture that gives the company 50 percent interest in the rehabilitation of a large oil field in southern Russia.

Black Sea, whose major shareholder is Canadian mining developer Robert Friedland, said the agreement covers the Anastasievsko-Troitskoye oil field, which has an estimated 190 million barrels in place.
It said about 53 million barrels were recoverable by the joint venture. Black's Sea's partner is Krasnodarneftegaz, a company controlled by Rosneftegaz.
The field, where 1,400 wells are available for rehabilitation, is connected by pipeline to Russia's main oil export terminal at the Black Sea port of Novorossiisk.
The company plans to use Canadian technology to boost output to 26,000 barrels of oil a day from the current 12,000.

The project was expected to require US$10 million for initial capital and operating costs. Startup is due later this year and includes the use of adavanced well completipon and horizontal drilling technology, Black Sea said.
John Ellis, who with Friedland is s co-chairman of Black Sea, was a financial adviser to the Russian oil ministry before directing international business development for Canadian Fracmaster Ltd.

Fracmaster was the first Canadian company to take oil in payment for reworking oil wells in Russia. Black Sea president Clint Hussin negotiated five joint ventures for Fracmaster. -- Reuters Calgary Bureau 403 531-1624
